name: Heat-lift and cool-down performance check of a tactical integral rotary Stirling cryocooler: 550 mW at 77 K at +71 C ambient, 5 min cool-down of a 250 J load to 80 K
plain_name: Check that a small battlefield-camera cooler can pull its heat load down to 77 K quickly
description: Performance acceptance of an integral rotary Stirling cooler for thermal-imaging focal planes, using the Ricor K508 ratings as test points: total cooling power 550 mW at a 77 K cold tip at 71 C ambient, cool-down of a 250 J thermal mass to 80 K in about 5 minutes at 23 C, cold-tip stability +/-0.5 K, all on DC electrical input power only.
keywords: Check that a small battlefield-camera cooler can pull its heat load down to 77 K quickly

sources.citation: Ricor K508 integral rotary Stirling cryocooler, product specification page

requirements.rationale: The cold tip is regulated at 77 K for the lift rating.
Required heat lift at 77 K (rated at +71 C ambient).
Tactical integral coolers run on DC electrical power alone, with no liquid cryogen.
Cool-down of a 250 J thermal mass to 80 K at 23 C in about 5 min (typical; depends on load mass).

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
